deep.reconstruction:
Folio 56v belongs to the drafts of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (1854/1867). The page has two unrelated columns.

RIGHT COLUMN: end of the proof of the paper's §8 'Satz 1', continuing the previous folio.

Setting (previous page). The trigonometric series is Ω = A_0/2 + Σ A_n, where A_n = a_n sin nx + b_n cos nx. Its partial sums are f(x)+ε_n, with ε_n → 0. Integrating twice termwise gives F(x) = C + C'x + A_0 x²/4 − Σ A_n/n².

(a) Termwise second difference. Since cos n(x+2α) + cos n(x−2α) − 2cos nx = −4 cos nx sin² nα (likewise for sin), one gets
[F(x+2α) − 2F(x) + F(x−2α)]/(4α²) = A_0/2 + Σ A_n (sin nα/(nα))².

(b) Abel summation. Put c_n = (sin nα/(nα))², c_0 = 1, and A_n = ε_n − ε_{n−1} (with the f(x) part split off). This gives
f(x) + Σ_{n≥1} ε_n [c_n − c_{n+1}].
The previous page splits this sum into three parts: n ≤ m, m < n ≤ s = ⌊π/α⌋, and n > s. Each part is shown to tend to 0 or to be ≤ const·δ.

(c) The page opens 'u. folglich convergirt' the quotient [F(x+2α) − 2Fx + F(x−2α)]/(4α²), i.e. the expression in (b), to f(x) as α → 0. This settles the case β = α.

(d) General case (written out here). Apply (c) with step (α+β)/2 and with step (α−β)/2:
- F(x+α+β) − 2Fx + F(x−α−β) = (fx + δ_1)(α+β)²
- F(x+α−β) − 2Fx + F(x−α+β) = (fx + δ_2)(α−β)²
Here δ_1, δ_2 → 0 as α, β → 0.

Subtracting the second line from the first:
F(x+α+β) − F(x+α−β) − F(x−α+β) + F(x−α−β) = 4αβ fx + (α+β)²δ_1 − (α−β)²δ_2.

Divide by 4αβ. The error term is [(α+β)²/(4αβ)]δ_1 − [(α−β)²/(4αβ)]δ_2. The coefficients stay bounded 'so lange β/α endlich bleibt'. Hence the error tends to 0, and the generalized quotient [F(x+α+β) − F(x+α−β) − F(x−α+β) + F(x−α−β)]/(4αβ) → f(x).

This is exactly the proof of Satz 1 in the published paper.

LEFT COLUMN: heavily struck-through drafts of the historical introduction (§§3–5 of the paper) on Dirichlet's work.

- Dirichlet's conditions are recalled. The page opens with the end of condition 3: at a discontinuity the function takes the mean of the two one-sided limits.
- Dirichlet thereby gave a firm foundation to a great many important analytic investigations. He clarified the point where Euler had gone wrong ('den Punkt, wo Euler … zur Klarheit brachte').
- Functions to which Dirichlet's investigation does not apply 'in der Natur nicht vorkommen'.
- If f satisfies the first two conditions but not the third, it cannot be represented by a trigonometric series. The series representing it elsewhere deviates from it at the discontinuities.
- If f is integrable throughout but has infinitely many maxima and minima, Dirichlet's argument fails. The integral (1/2π)∫_{−π}^{π} f(x) sin((2n+1)(x−α)/2)/sin((x−α)/2) dx could, for n → ∞, tend to a finite value different from (f(α+0)+f(α−0))/2. So representability remains undecided by Dirichlet's method.
- Whether, and when, a function not satisfying the first two conditions is representable is likewise left open.
- This circumstance 'prescribes the course of the following investigation', which cannot simply follow Dirichlet's procedure.
errors: No mathematical error in the right-column derivation; the algebraic identity is exact.

Implicit requirement (not a slip, but worth stating): 'ratio finite' must mean β/α is bounded and bounded away from 0. If β/α → 0, the coefficient (α+β)²/(4αβ) blows up. Riemann's phrase 'nicht unendlich gross werden … so lange β/α endlich bleibt' covers this only if 'endlich' excludes 0 as well as ∞.
When α = β the δ_2 line is degenerate (the step is 0). Its coefficient (α−β)² vanishes, so no harm results.

results.what: If the trigonometric series converges at x to f(x), then the second symmetric difference quotient of the twice-integrated series F converges to f(x). More generally, the mixed quotient Δ_{α,β}F/(4αβ) → f(x) when β/α stays bounded above and below.
results.modern_name: Riemann's first lemma (Riemann's theorem on the Schwarz/Riemann second symmetric derivative of the Riemann function F)

results.what: Abel summation with kernel (sin nα/nα)², split into three ranges of n
results.modern_name: Riemann summability method / Abel partial summation

results.what: Historical discussion of Dirichlet's conditions and of the Dirichlet kernel integral; integrable functions with infinitely many maxima and minima left undecided
results.modern_name: Dirichlet's theorem on Fourier series convergence (Dirichlet conditions)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material published essentially verbatim in Riemann's Habilitationsschrift (Satz 1 and the Dirichlet history). It is of interest only for the drafting process.

checkable.asserts: Termwise second difference of −cos(nx)/n² gives cos(nx)(sin nα/nα)² (result should be 0).
Mixed difference quotient termwise gives sin nα sin nβ/(nα nβ) (should be 0).
Algebraic identity of the right column (should be 0).
The coefficient blows up (oo) when β/α = t → 0, showing the ratio must be bounded away from 0.

transcription_corrections: The Dirichlet integral should read (1/2π)∫_{−π}^{π} f(x) sin((2n+1)(x−α)/2) / sin((x−α)/2) dx. The denominator sin((x−α)/2) is written below the line and is omitted in the transcription.
'einen endlichen Grössenwerth von (f(x+0)+f(x−0))/2 verschieden' is more plausibly 'einen endlichen, von (f(α+0)+f(α−0))/2 verschiedenen Grenzwerth' (the evaluation point is α).
The right column's first formula should read Σ_{1,∞} ε_n[(sin nα/nα)² − (sin(n+1)α/((n+1)α))²]; the transcription is correct. The garbled phrase before it is likely 'mit abnehmendem α gegen fx'.

Left column: 'Dirichlet's Untersuchung' near the top more likely reads 'durch Dirichlet's Untersuchung unentschieden bleibt' (struck), in the sentence 'dass die Functionen, deren Darstellbarkeit … unentschieden lässt, in der Natur nicht vorkommen'.
